programmes.name: Antigua & Barbuda Citizenship by Investment
programmes.cardSummary: An independent Commonwealth nation in the Eastern Caribbean, comprising the islands of Antigua and Barbuda.
programmes.overview:
Citizenship of Antigua & Barbuda can be obtained through a contribution (Option 1 or 2), an approved real estate investment (Option 3) or an approved business investment (Option 4), with qualifying family members included in a single application. The programme is administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU).
9–12 months*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
5 days: Minimum stay required in any five-year period after citizenship.
5 years: Minimum holding period for the real estate route.
144†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 7 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access page for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Children aged 0 to 30 who are financially dependent on the main applicant
Children aged 18 or over who are disabled, live with and are fully supported by the main applicant
A parent or grandparent of the main applicant or spouse, aged 55 or over and financially dependent on the main applicant
An unmarried sibling of the main applicant or spouse
Investment Routes
Option 1 — National Development Fund
Make a non-refundable contribution of US$230,000 per application. A spouse, dependent children and dependent parents over 55 may be included without an additional NDF contribution.
Option 2 — UWI Fund
Contribute US$260,000, including processing fees, for a minimum of six persons, plus US$10,000 for each additional dependant. One family member receives a one-year scholarship covering tuition only at the University of the West Indies.
For both contribution options, payment is due within 30 days of the approval letter.
Investment Options
Option 3 — Approved Real Estate
Purchase property worth at least US$300,000 in an approved project, supported by a binding purchase agreement. The property must be held for five years unless another officially approved property in Antigua and Barbuda is purchased.
Option 4 — Approved Business
Invest at least US$1,500,000 individually in an approved business, or make a joint investment of at least US$5,000,000 with two or more investors, each contributing a minimum of US$400,000.

[/TABLE]

All Options (US$)

Main applicant | US$8,500

programmes.name: Dominica Citizenship by Investment
programmes.cardSummary: An independent Commonwealth island state in the Eastern Caribbean, situated between Guadeloupe and Martinique.
programmes.overview:
Citizenship of Dominica can be obtained through a contribution to the Economic Diversification Fund (Option 1) or an approved real estate investment (Option 2), with qualifying family members included in a single application. The programme is administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CBIU), and applications are submitted only through authorised agents.
9–12 months*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement‡: Applicants do not have to reside in Dominica before or after citizenship is granted.
3 or 5 years: Holding period for the real estate route, depending on whether the subsequent buyer applies for citizenship.
135†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 8 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access section for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
‡ CBIU FAQs: applicants do not have to reside in Dominica before or after citizenship is granted.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
A child under 18 of the main applicant or spouse
A child aged 18 to 30 of the main applicant or spouse, in higher education and fully supported; a child who has turned 31 cannot be included
An unmarried daughter under 25, living with and fully supported by the main applicant
A child aged 18 or over with a physical or mental disability who is fully supported
Parents or grandparents over 65 who are substantially supported
Good to Know
The main applicant must be at least 18 years old.
A mandatory interview applies to applicants aged 16 or over, usually conducted virtually.
Some nationalities are banned, suspended or restricted: see the nationality restrictions below.
Dominica permits dual citizenship, with no requirement to renounce another citizenship.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Economic Diversification Fund
Make a non-refundable contribution of US$200,000 for a single applicant, or US$250,000 for the main applicant and up to three qualifying dependants. The Economic Diversification Fund (EDF) supports Dominica’s economic growth and diversification.
For each dependant beyond the main applicant and three dependants, an additional contribution applies:
[TABLE]
Dependant | Additional contribution
Each additional dependant under 18 | US$25,000
Each additional dependant aged 18 or over | US$40,000
[/TABLE]
The contribution is made after approval in principle, through an authorised agent. No separate route-specific government fee applies to the EDF contribution; application and due diligence fees are listed below.
Investment Options
Option 2 — Approved Real Estate
Purchase property worth at least US$200,000 in a government-approved real estate project, such as a resort or residence. Government fees start from US$75,000 and are payable after approval, in addition to the investment.
The property must be held for at least three years before it can be sold to a buyer who is not applying for citizenship. A five-year holding period applies before it can be sold to a buyer who will apply for citizenship through the property.
Nationality Restrictions
Banned: Belarus, Russia, and Northern Iraq (nationals of Erbil, Amedi, Dahuk, Kirkuk, Lalish, Raniya, Soran, Sulaymaniyah and Zakho).
Suspended: Yemen.
Restricted: Applications from nationals of Iran, North Korea and Sudan are refused unless the applicant meets all of the following conditions:
Has not lived in the country for at least ten years
Holds no substantial assets there
Has conducted no business or similar activity in or with the country
Enhanced due diligence is conducted on all Iranian applicants and may apply to other applicants who meet the conditions above, at the applicant’s cost.
Government Processing Fees
Option 2 — Approved Real Estate (US$)
The following government fees are payable after approval, in addition to the property investment.
[TABLE]
Family | Government fee
Single applicant | US$75,000
Main applicant and up to three dependants | US$100,000
Each additional dependant under 18, beyond the main applicant and three dependants | US$25,000
Each additional dependant aged 18 or over, beyond the main applicant and three dependants | US$40,000
[/TABLE]
Application Fees — All Options (US$)
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Processing fee | US$1,000 per application
Interview fee | US$1,000 per interview, for each applicant aged 16 or over
Certificate of Naturalisation | US$500 per person
[/TABLE]
Due Diligence Fees
All Options (US$)
[TABLE]
Applicant | Fee
Main applicant | US$7,500
Each dependant aged 16 or over | US$4,000
[/TABLE]
Enhanced due diligence fees may apply depending on citizenship status and personal circumstances.
Passport fee (all options): US$300 per person.
Payments may be made in USD, EUR or GBP. Elevay professional fees are provided upon request. All government and Elevay fees are subject to change without notice.
Additional Country Information
Independence: Dominica gained independence from the United Kingdom on 3 November 1978.
Dual citizenship: Permitted; applicants are not required to renounce another citizenship.
Tax: According to the programme site, Dominica has no wealth, gift, inheritance, foreign income or capital gains tax. Citizens who reside in Dominica pay personal tax. Tax treatment depends on individual circumstances; independent tax advice should be obtained.
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Sources, all accessed 8 October 2026: cbiu.gov.dm (Facts; FAQs; Benefits); World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD); IANA time zone database (America/Dominica).

programmes.name: Egypt Citizenship by Investment
programmes.cardSummary: A country in North Africa, with citizenship available to qualifying foreign investors under Law No. 140 of 2019.
programmes.overview:
Egyptian citizenship can be granted by the Prime Minister through a property purchase (Option 1), an investment project (Option 2), a cash deposit (Option 3) or a direct revenue payment to the government (Option 4). Qualifying family members may also obtain citizenship, subject to the conditions below. Applications are submitted to the Egyptian Citizenship by Investment unit, directly or through licensed intermediaries.
9–12 months*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement: A six-month temporary residence is available as an option during the application.
5 years: Holding period for the property and investment project routes.
3 years: Holding period for the cash deposit route.
61†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. The official programme site states 6–12 months. This is not a guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 8 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access section for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant, with no additional application fee. The spouse can apply after two years of marriage, counted from the issue of the main applicant’s Egyptian citizenship.
Children under 21.
Good to Know
All nationalities may apply. National security agencies are consulted on every application.
There is no language test, so knowledge of Arabic is not required.
Egyptian law permits dual citizenship, although other countries may restrict it.
Children who obtain citizenship by investment are not required to perform military service, according to the official programme FAQs.
There is no residence requirement.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Property Purchase
Purchase property worth at least US$300,000, with funds transferred from abroad. The property must be held for five years. If it is sold within that period, retaining citizenship requires a non-refundable payment of US$250,000 to the state treasury through the Central Bank of Egypt.
Option 2 — Investment Project
Invest at least US$350,000, transferred from abroad, in a project that meets Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, plus a US$100,000 donation to the government.
The investment must be maintained for five years of operation. If the project is liquidated or the holding is disposed of within that period, a further non-refundable payment of US$250,000 is due.
Investment Options
Option 3 — Cash Deposit
Deposit US$500,000 by foreign bank transfer into a special account at the Central Bank of Egypt for three years. The deposit is returned in Egyptian pounds at the Central Bank exchange rate on the refund date, without interest.
Option 4 — Direct Revenue Payment
Make a non-refundable payment of US$250,000 by foreign bank transfer as direct revenue to the government. Payment can be made in instalments over no more than one year.
Neither the cash deposit route nor the direct revenue route requires a property purchase or business investment.
Payment by Instalments
The US$300,000 property route and the US$250,000 direct revenue route can be paid in instalments over no more than one year. Citizenship is granted only after full payment, and the applicant receives a temporary non-tourist residence during that time.
If payment is not completed or the application is withdrawn, amounts paid are refunded in Egyptian pounds at the Central Bank exchange rate on the refund date, capped at the rate on the payment date, without interest.
Government Processing Fees
All Options (US$)
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Application fee | US$10,000 per application, non-refundable
[/TABLE]
The fee is paid by bank transfer from abroad, or by depositing the amount at a customs port and transferring it to the designated account.
Elevay professional fees are provided upon request. All government and Elevay fees are subject to change without notice.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is required. National security agencies are consulted on every application.
How the Application Works
Submit the application: Provide the application and supporting documents in person at the unit’s office in Cairo or through licensed immigration intermediaries.
Pay the application fee: Pay the non-refundable US$10,000 fee.
Application review: The unit confirms receipt within three working days, reviews the file and issues a preliminary decision.
Complete the investment: Following the Prime Minister’s preliminary approval, complete the chosen investment route. A six-month temporary residence is available as an option; residence is not required.
Receive citizenship: The Prime Minister issues the final decision, and citizenship is granted through a certificate of naturalisation.
Legal Basis
Law No. 140 of 2019 allows the Prime Minister to grant Egyptian citizenship to foreigners. Grants are regulated by Prime Minister Decisions No. 3099 of 2019 and No. 3562 of 2023. The Cabinet unit reviewing applications was formed by Decision No. 647 of 2020.
Citizenship can be revoked within ten years if obtained through fraud or false statements.
Country Information Sources
Sources, all accessed 8 October 2026: Constitution of Egypt, Articles 2 and 222 (constituteproject.org); World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); ecu.gov.eg.
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.

programmes.overview:
Citizenship of Grenada can be obtained through a contribution to the National Transformation Fund (Option 1) or an approved real estate investment (Option 2 or 3), with qualifying family members included in a single application. The programme is administered by the Investment Migration Agency (IMA) Grenada, and applications are submitted through authorised agents.
6–9 months*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No visit required‡: Applicants do not need to visit Grenada to apply.
5 years: Minimum holding period for the real estate routes.
139†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.

‡ IMA Grenada FAQ. As stated in the supplied source material, IMA Circular No. 2 of 2026 announces a regional residence requirement that has not yet taken effect; details have not been published.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Children under 18, and children aged 18 to under 30 who are supported by the main applicant
Children aged 18 or over with a physical or mental disability who live with and are fully supported by the main applicant
A parent or grandparent of the main applicant or spouse who is fully supported by the main applicant
An unmarried sibling of the main applicant or spouse, aged 18 or over, with no children
A child born within 12 months of the grant of citizenship
Good to Know
The main applicant must be at least 18 years old, in good health and able to demonstrate a legal source of funds.
A mandatory online interview forms part of due diligence.
Applications must be submitted through an authorised agent.
Some nationalities are ineligible or restricted: see the nationality restrictions below.
Grenada permits dual citizenship, with no requirement to renounce another citizenship or passport.
All fees are non-refundable.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — National Transformation Fund
Make a one-time, non-refundable contribution of US$235,000 for a single applicant or the main applicant and up to three dependants. The National Transformation Fund (NTF) finances projects that support Grenada’s economy and diversification.
The contribution is made through an authorised local agent. Applicants may apply for citizenship immediately, or first apply for permanent residence and apply for citizenship later.
Additional dependant contributions are listed below.
Investment Options
Option 2 — Approved Real Estate
Invest at least US$350,000 in an approved real estate project, plus a US$50,000 government contribution for the main applicant and up to three dependants.
Option 3 — Shared Tourism Accommodation Unit
Invest at least US$270,000 per share in an approved tourism accommodation unit purchased jointly by two or more investors, plus a US$50,000 government contribution for the main applicant and up to three dependants.
For both real estate options, the project must be approved by the Minister and published in the Gazette. Investments are made through an authorised local agent, typically in approved hotels, resorts or villas.
The investment must be held for at least five years after citizenship is granted.

Nationals residing in Iran, North Korea, Russia, Belarus, Sudan, Yemen and Afghanistan are ineligible, without exception.
Nationals of Iran, Sudan, Yemen and Afghanistan may apply only if they meet the following conditions:
Migrated before the age of majority and/or have held permanent residence or a valid visa in Canada, the United Kingdom, a Schengen state, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Saudi Arabia or the United Arab Emirates for at least ten years

All Options (US$)

Applicant | Fee

Child aged 0 to 16 | US$0
[/TABLE]
Enhanced due diligence may apply to eligible applicants from restricted countries at a significantly higher cost.

programmes.overview:
Citizenship of Saint Lucia can be obtained through a contribution to the National Economic Fund (Option 1), the purchase of a National Action Bond (Option 2), or an investment in an approved real estate or enterprise project (Option 3 or 4), with qualifying family members included in a single application. The programme is administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU), and applications are submitted through authorised agents.
12–18 months*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement‡: No residence requirement applies under the cited legislation.

137†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.

Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Children aged 21 or under, and children up to 30 who are fully supported by the main applicant
Children of any age with a physical or mental disability who are fully supported
Parents over 55 who are fully supported by the main applicant
Parents of any age with a physical or mental disability who are fully supported
Unmarried siblings under 18, with parental consent
Good to Know
Due diligence is conducted only on applicants above the age of 16.
An applicant interview and identity verification process applies to all applications. The fee is payable by the main applicant only.
Applications must be submitted through an authorised agent.
Saint Lucia permits dual citizenship, with no requirement to renounce another citizenship.
Sources: cipsaintlucia.com (Citizenship by Investment; FAQs), Citizenship by Investment Act, Cap. 1.20, accessed 7 October 2026.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — National Economic Fund
Contribute US$240,000 to the National Economic Fund (NEF) for a single applicant or the main applicant and up to three dependants. The fund finances projects benefiting Saint Lucia’s economy. No holding period applies.
The contribution is made through an authorised agent.
Additional NEF Contributions (US$)
[TABLE]
Dependant category | Contribution
Additional dependant under 18 | US$10,000 each
Additional dependant aged 18 or over | US$20,000 each
Newborn aged 12 months or under | US$5,000
Spouse | US$35,000
Other qualifying dependants | US$25,000 each
[/TABLE]
Option 2 — National Action Bond
Purchase a National Action Bond (NAB) worth US$300,000 for the main applicant and any number of dependants, plus a non-refundable fee of US$50,000.
The bond is issued by the Government of Saint Lucia and must be held for five years from the date of first issue. Applications are made through an authorised agent.
Investment Options
Option 3 — Approved Real Estate
Invest at least US$300,000 in an approved high-end branded hotel or resort with 70 or more rooms, or a boutique property with 20 to 70 rooms. Administration fees apply in addition to the investment.
The investment must be held for at least five years.
Option 4 — Approved Enterprise Project
Invest in an approved enterprise project through one of the following arrangements:
Sole developer: Invest at least US$3,500,000 and create at least three permanent jobs, plus a US$50,000 fee.
Joint venture: Make a combined investment of at least US$6,000,000, with each investor contributing at least US$1,000,000, and create at least six permanent jobs, plus a US$50,000 fee.
Enterprise project with dependants: Invest from US$250,000, plus the administration fees listed below.
Enterprise investments must be held for at least five years.
Real estate and enterprise projects must be approved by the CIU and demonstrate viable commercial, operational and financial proposals.
Sources: cipsaintlucia.com (Citizenship by Investment; FAQs; Get a Real Estate Project Approved; Get an Enterprise Project Approved), Citizenship by Investment Act, Cap. 1.20, accessed 7 October 2026.

Applicant category | Fee

Applicant with three dependants | US$30,000
Each additional dependant | US$10,000
[/TABLE]
Application fees apply in addition to the route-specific fees above.

Applicant | Fee

Each dependant above the age of 16 | US$5,000

The programme operates under Nationality Law No. 07/2022 and Decree-Law No. 07/2025. According to the programme site, citizenship acquired through the programme carries no distinction from citizenship by birth.
60–90 days*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement: Applicants are not required to reside in São Tomé and Príncipe.
No holding period: The programme uses a contribution route; no asset is purchased.
70†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 8 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access section for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant, through a monogamous marriage or de facto partnership
Unmarried children up to 30 years old
Parents and grandparents aged 55 or over
Qualifying dependants may be included in the original application or added after approval in principle, subject to the inclusion fees listed below.
Good to Know
The main applicant must be at least 18 years old.
There is no residence requirement.
Applicants are not required to give up their existing nationality.
According to the programme site, citizenship can be passed to all future generations.
All amounts shown are in US dollars.
Sources: cip.gov.st (programme; Qualifying Dependents; Benefits of Citizenship pages, as supplied by Elevay), accessed 4 and 9 October 2026.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — National Transformation Fund
Contribute US$90,000 for a single applicant or US$95,000 for a family of two to four, plus US$5,000 for each additional dependant.
The minimum contribution is due on approval in principle. This is the programme’s only investment route. Submission and citizenship document fees apply in addition to the contribution.
Contribution Amounts (US$)
[TABLE]
Applicants | Contribution
Single applicant | US$90,000
Family of two to four | US$95,000
Each additional dependant | US$5,000
[/TABLE]
Sources: cip.gov.st (programme; Benefits pages, as supplied by Elevay), accessed 4 October 2026.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Submission fee | US$5,000 per application, regardless of family size
Citizenship documents: Certificate of Registration, passport and national ID | US$750 per applicant
[/TABLE]
Inclusion Fees for Dependants Added After Approval in Principle
Qualifying dependants may be added after approval in principle for the following fees.
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Submission fee | US$5,000; not charged for newborns
Spouse | US$10,000
Each additional dependant | US$5,000
Newborn up to one year old | US$500
[/TABLE]
Elevay professional fees are provided upon request. All government and Elevay fees are subject to change without notice and depend on the number of applicants and the complexity of the process.
According to the supplied programme information, no government fees apply beyond those listed in this summary.
Sources: cip.gov.st (programme; Benefits pages, as supplied by Elevay), accessed 4 October 2026.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is required.
The passport is included in the US$750 citizenship document fee per applicant, together with the Certificate of Registration and national ID.
Additional Country Information
Dual citizenship: According to the programme site, applicants are not required to give up their existing nationality, and citizenship can be passed to all future generations.
Citizenship status: The programme site states that citizenship acquired through the programme carries no distinction from citizenship by birth.
Legal basis: Nationality Law No. 07/2022 and Decree-Law No. 07/2025.
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Country information sources, accessed 8 and 9 October 2026: Constitution of São Tomé and Príncipe, Article 5 (constituteproject.org); Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe (bcstp.st); cip.gov.st (FAQ; Benefits of Citizenship, screenshots supplied by Elevay, accessed 9 October 2026); World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

programmes.name: Türkiye Citizenship by Investment
programmes.cardSummary: A country spanning Europe and Asia, where qualifying investors can apply for citizenship through real estate or capital investment.
programmes.overview:
A qualifying investment in Türkiye allows an investor to apply for Turkish citizenship through real estate (Option 1) or capital investment (Options 2 to 5), with the spouse and children under 18 applying together with the main applicant. Every application is decided by the President of the Republic of Türkiye, and approval is not guaranteed.
9–12 months*: Estimated time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement: Applicants are not required to reside in Türkiye.
3 years‡: Minimum investment holding period.
121†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 4 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access section for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
‡ The three-year holding period for the fixed capital route is based on Elevay management confirmation. The official sources cited in the supplied material do not state a holding period for that route.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Children under 18
Included family members apply together with the main applicant.
Good to Know
Türkiye permits dual citizenship, according to Elevay management confirmation.
There is no requirement to reside in Türkiye, but obtaining a residence permit forms part of the application process.
The chosen investment must be attested by the relevant authority.
Applications undergo an archive check concerning national security and public order.
The President makes the final decision; a qualifying investment does not guarantee citizenship.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Real Estate
Purchase real estate in Türkiye worth at least US$400,000. The property must not be sold for three years, and a restriction is placed on the title deed.
The investment is attested by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change.
Investment Options
Option 2 — Fixed Capital Investment
Make a fixed capital investment of at least US$500,000 or equivalent, attested by the Ministry of Industry and Technology.
A three-year holding period is stated by Elevay management; the official sources cited in the supplied material do not specify a period for this route.
Option 3 — Bank Deposit
Deposit at least US$500,000 or equivalent in banks operating in Türkiye. The funds must not be withdrawn for at least three years.
The investment is attested by the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BRSA).
Option 4 — Government Bonds
Invest at least US$500,000 or equivalent in government bonds. The bonds must not be sold for at least three years.
The investment is attested by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance.
Option 5 — Real Estate or Venture Capital Fund Shares
Invest at least US$500,000 or equivalent in real estate or venture capital fund shares. The shares must not be sold for at least three years.
The investment is attested by the Capital Markets Board (SPK).
Investment amounts are converted using the Central Bank of Türkiye’s effective selling or cross rate on the determination date. No contribution route is required.
Sources: invest.gov.tr, Acquiring Property and Citizenship (updated 11 August 2026); the official invest.gov.tr guide (current as of 1 January 2024); spk.gov.tr (fund shares route), accessed 9 October 2026. Fixed capital holding period: Elevay management confirmation, 9 October 2026.
Government Processing Fees
All Options (US$)
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Government fee | US$1,000 per person
[/TABLE]
Additional Real Estate Costs
Budget approximately 5% to 7% for the cost of transferring the property into your name, plus insurance. This is an Elevay budgeting estimate, not a government-published figure.
Fees may change. Confirm the current figures with your Elevay consultant before applying.
Government fee and property transfer costs: Elevay management confirmation, 9 October 2026.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is required.
Applications remain subject to an archive check concerning national security and public order.
How the Application Works
Obtain a certificate of eligibility: Secure confirmation from the authority responsible for attesting the chosen investment route.
Obtain a residence permit: Apply under Law No. 6458, Article 31(j), at the Provincial Directorate of Immigration Administration.
Submit the citizenship application: Apply at the Provincial Directorate of Census and Citizenship.
Complete the archive check: The file is sent to NVIGM for checks concerning national security and public order.
Receive the decision: The President decides on the application. Approval is not guaranteed.
Sources: invest.gov.tr, Acquiring Property and Citizenship (updated 11 August 2026); the official invest.gov.tr guide (current as of 1 January 2024), accessed 9 October 2026. Processing time, residence requirement, holding period, children’s age limit and dual citizenship: Elevay management confirmation, 9 October 2026.
Country Information Sources
Sources, all accessed 9 October 2026: World Bank Open Data (population, surface area and GDP per capita); Constitution of the Republic of Türkiye, Article 3; Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (tcmb.gov.tr, Turkish Lira Sign).
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.

programmes.name: Vanuatu Citizenship by Investment
programmes.cardSummary: A Pacific country offering honorary citizenship through a non-refundable contribution to its Development Support Program.
programmes.overview:
Vanuatu grants honorary citizenship through a non-refundable contribution to its Development Support Program (DSP), with qualifying family members included in a single application. Applications are reviewed and approved by the Vanuatu Citizenship Commission.
60–90 days*: Typical time to citizenship, based on current Elevay files.
No residence requirement: Applicants are not required to reside in Vanuatu.
No holding period: The programme uses a non-refundable contribution route.
93†: Visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.
* Based on Elevay’s experience processing current files. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline and varies by case.
† Passport Index, accessed 8 October 2026. Indicative only: see the passport access section for the breakdown, sources and important notice.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Dependent children up to the age of 25
Dependent parents of the main applicant or spouse, aged 50 or over
Good to Know
There is no residence requirement.
Vanuatu recognises dual citizenship under its amended Citizenship Act, although other countries may restrict it.
Citizenship under the DSP is described as honorary citizenship.
Applications are subject to screening and approval by the Vanuatu Citizenship Commission.
Contributions and fees are set in US dollars.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Development Support Program
Make a non-refundable contribution to the Development Support Program, starting at US$130,000 for a single applicant. The contribution depends on the number of family members included in the application.
Subject to screening and approval by the Vanuatu Citizenship Commission, the main applicant and qualifying family members are granted honorary citizenship under the programme.
Contribution Amounts (US$)
[TABLE]
Applicants | Non-refundable contribution
Single applicant | US$130,000
Married couple | US$150,000
Married couple and one child | US$165,000
Married couple and two children | US$180,000
Each additional applicant | US$10,000
[/TABLE]
This is the programme’s only route described in this summary. Due diligence and passport delivery fees apply in addition to the contribution.
Sources: vancitizenship.gov.vu (Fees and Charges; Types of Citizenship; News and Updates), accessed 8 October 2026.
Government Processing Fees
Other Fees (US$)
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Passport delivery | US$5,000
[/TABLE]
Elevay professional fees are provided upon request.
Due Diligence Fees
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Due diligence fee (FIU) | US$5,000
[/TABLE]
All government and Elevay fees are subject to change without notice. Fees depend on the number of applicants and the complexity of the process.
Sources: vancitizenship.gov.vu (Fees and Charges; Types of Citizenship), accessed 8 October 2026.
Additional Country Information
Dual citizenship: Vanuatu recognises dual citizenship. A citizen of Vanuatu or another state may be granted dual citizenship, although other countries may restrict it.
Legal basis: Citizenship is granted under the Citizenship Act [Cap 112]. Honorary citizenship is provided for in Section 20, and the Citizenship (Development Support Program) Regulations are published as Order No. 33 of 2019.
Tax Information
The Vanuatu Foreign Investment Promotion Agency publishes the following tax information:
[TABLE]
Tax | Treatment
Personal income tax | None
Corporate tax | Zero, except on some real estate transactions
Capital gains tax | None
Withholding tax | None
VAT | 15%
[/TABLE]
Tax treatment in your country of residence is separate and depends on your circumstances. Elevay does not provide tax advice; independent advice should be obtained before applying.
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Sources, all accessed 8 October 2026: Constitution of Vanuatu, Article 3 (constituteproject.org); World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, AG.SRF.TOTL.K2 and country record); vancitizenship.gov.vu; investvanuatu.vu (Low-tax jurisdiction).

programmes.name: Canada Provincial Entrepreneur Pathways
programmes.cardSummary: A North American country offering provincial entrepreneur pathways for applicants who live in the province and actively manage a business.
programmes.overview:
Provincial entrepreneur streams provide a pathway towards Canadian permanent residence for qualifying business owners who establish or acquire a business and actively manage it in the province. This summary covers British Columbia, Alberta, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Newfoundland and Labrador.
Applicants must meet the relevant province’s business and residence conditions before nomination can follow. A separate federal permanent residence application follows provincial nomination. Several streams operate through invitations or selection, and an invitation, nomination or approval is not guaranteed.
5 provinces: Six entrepreneur streams covered, including two in British Columbia.
Mandatory provincial stay: Applicants must live in the province and actively operate the business.
From CAD 100,000: Lowest minimum investment among the streams covered, depending on the stream and location.
About 13 months*: Federal processing stage after nomination; this is not the total programme timeline.
* IRCC processing time for non-Express Entry provincial nominee applications, as at 9 October 2026. Times change monthly and are not guaranteed. Provincial selection, work permit processing and business establishment take additional time.
CAD means Canadian dollar. CLB means Canadian Language Benchmarks. IRCC means Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.
Who Can Be Included
Under the federal family definitions, qualifying family members include:
The spouse of the main applicant
A common-law partner who has lived with the main applicant in a conjugal relationship for at least one year
Dependent children of the main applicant or spouse or common-law partner who are under 22 and are not married or in a common-law partnership
Children aged 22 or over who have depended on a parent’s financial support since before turning 22 and cannot support themselves because of a physical or mental condition
Dependent children of a dependent child
Provinces may impose additional conditions. Other relatives are not covered by these definitions. Your Elevay consultant will confirm who qualifies in your case.
For the Nova Scotia Entrepreneur Stream, an accompanying spouse or common-law partner must demonstrate language ability of at least CLB 4. All dependants must be declared in the application, including those who will not immigrate.
Source: Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, sections 1 and 2, accessed 20 October 2026. Federal family definitions.
Investment Routes
Each province sets its own eligibility criteria, eligible investment rules and business performance conditions.
Option 1 — British Columbia Entrepreneur Immigration: Base Stream
Make an eligible personal investment of at least CAD 200,000 in a business and demonstrate a personal net worth of at least CAD 600,000.
Experience: At least three years as a business owner-manager within the last ten years; the programme summary states that an eligible education credential can substitute.
Jobs: Create at least one new full-time job for a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.
Language: CLB 4.
Intake status: Open by invitation, according to the cited programme information. The latest draw cited, dated 22 September 2026, issued ten Base Stream invitations with a minimum score of 119.
Mandatory Stay And Business Operation
After approval, sign a Performance Agreement and receive a Letter of Support for a work permit. Apply for the work permit within 90 days and arrive in British Columbia within 12 months of receiving it.
Applicants have up to 20 months after arrival to implement the business plan and actively manage the business. A final report is submitted 18–20 months after arrival. Nomination follows only if the Performance Agreement is met.
Processing Time
British Columbia reports that approximately 80% of cases are processed within the following periods:
[TABLE]
Stage | Estimated time
Registration score notification | 6 weeks
Application decision — work permit stage | 4 months
Application decision — final report stage | 4 months
Request for review | 6 months
[/TABLE]
These are provincial estimates, not guarantees.
Option 2 — British Columbia Entrepreneur Immigration: Regional Stream
Make an eligible investment of at least CAD 100,000 and demonstrate a personal net worth of at least CAD 300,000.
Location: Establish a business outside the Metro Vancouver Regional District, aligned with a participating community’s priorities.
Community requirements: Complete an exploratory visit and obtain a community referral form.
Experience: At least three years as an owner-manager within the last five years.
Jobs: Create at least one new full-time job.
Language: CLB 4.
Intake status: Open by invitation, according to the cited programme information. The 22 September 2026 draw issued fewer than five Regional Stream invitations with a minimum score of 119.
A stay in British Columbia and active business operation are required. The Regional Stream’s arrival and performance timeline is not specified in the supplied summary.
Sources for both British Columbia streams: WelcomeBC, accessed 20 October 2026. Entrepreneur immigration; Invitations to apply.
Option 3 — Alberta Rural Entrepreneur Stream
Invest at least CAD 100,000 from your own equity and/or that of your spouse or partner, and demonstrate a minimum net worth of CAD 300,000.
Ownership: At least 51% of a new business, or 100% for a business succession.
Experience: At least three years as an active owner-manager or four years as a senior manager within the last ten years.
Location: A rural community with fewer than 100,000 people, outside the Calgary and Edmonton areas.
Language: CLB 4.
Before applying: Complete an exploratory visit and obtain a Community Support Letter before submitting an Expression of Interest.
Intake status: Listed as open in the supplied summary. Its review of Alberta’s immigration updates found unchanged eligibility criteria and no intake pause.
Mandatory Stay And Business Operation
Approved applicants sign a Business Performance Agreement and receive a Letter of Support for a two-year work permit.
To qualify for nomination, applicants must operate the business in the rural community for at least 12 months, meet the agreement and demonstrate that the business is generating products or services after one year.
After nomination, apply to IRCC within six months.
Processing Time
Alberta does not publish a processing time for its entrepreneur streams. Timelines vary as applications pass through several review stages.
Sources: Government of Alberta, accessed 20 October 2026. Programme updates; Eligibility; How to apply; Processing information.
Option 4 — Nova Scotia Entrepreneur Stream
Make a personal investment of at least CAD 150,000 and demonstrate a minimum net worth of CAD 600,000. Outside Halifax Regional Municipality, the minimums are CAD 100,000 for investment and CAD 400,000 for net worth.
Age: At least 21.
Experience: At least three years running a business with a minimum one-third ownership, or more than five years in senior management.
Language: CLB 5.
Accompanying spouse or partner: At least CLB 4.
Family declaration: Include all dependants in the application, even those who will not immigrate.
Intake status: Active by invitation only, according to the programme page updated 6 August 2026. Recent invitation rounds were not reviewed in the supplied summary.
Mandatory Stay And Business Operation
Applicants must live permanently in Nova Scotia and actively manage the business day to day. After operating the business for one year, they may be nominated.
Processing Time
Nova Scotia does not publish an Entrepreneur Stream processing time. Its guide provides no fixed timeline for assessing applications or selecting Expressions of Interest.
Sources: Nova Scotia Provincial Nominee Program, accessed 20 October 2026. Entrepreneur Stream; Programme guide.
Option 5 — New Brunswick Business Immigration
Make an eligible investment of at least CAD 150,000 and demonstrate a personal net worth of at least CAD 500,000, or CAD 300,000 for agriculture.
Jobs: The business plan must create at least one new full-time job.
Management: Run the business and participate in daily management.
Ownership or role: Ownership of at least 51%, or a senior management role.
Employees: Supervise at least two employees.
Language: Requirements are not specified in the supplied summary; your Elevay consultant will confirm.
Intake status: Described as current and active on the official page reviewed for the supplied summary. No pause notice was found; the page and March 2025 guide did not provide an intake date.
Mandatory Stay And Business Operation
The Business Establishment Period lasts 24 months from arrival. Applicants must:
Open the business within nine months of arrival
Operate the business for one year within the 24-month period
Live in New Brunswick for 75% of the period and within 100 km of the business
Submit a Report of Arrival within one month of arrival
Sign the Business Performance Agreement within 60 days of the work permit support letter
The supplied March 2025 guide also states that nomination may be requested after at least six consecutive months of business operation.
Processing Time
New Brunswick does not publish a processing time for assessment or the nomination decision.
Sources: Government of New Brunswick, accessed 20 October 2026. Business Immigration Stream; March 2025 stream guide.
Option 6 — Newfoundland And Labrador International Entrepreneur
Demonstrate CAD 600,000 in personal and business assets that can be transferred to Canada. Invest at least CAD 200,000 in a business with at least 33.3% ownership, or CAD 1 million in equity.
Age: 21–59.
Experience: At least two years of business ownership and management, with at least 25% ownership, within the last five years; or at least five years in senior management within the last ten years.
Jobs: Create at least one full-time job for a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.
Language: CLB 5.
Exploratory visit: Required when applying from outside the province.
Excluded businesses: Remote, passive-investment and property-rental businesses.
Intake status: The official page updated 4 May 2026 states that the Expression of Interest system is open.
Mandatory Stay And Business Operation
Start or purchase a business in the province, actively manage it every day and operate it for at least one full year. Applicants who meet the requirements may be nominated for permanent residence.
Processing Time
Newfoundland and Labrador states that it does not currently have standard processing times for its provincial nominee programme.
Sources: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, International Entrepreneur overview, eligibility criteria and candidate FAQs, accessed 20 October 2026. Provincial immigration information.
Federal Processing After Nomination
Following provincial nomination, applicants proceed to the federal permanent residence stage.
IRCC reports approximately 13 months for non-Express Entry provincial nominee applications, as at 9 October 2026. Processing times change monthly and are not guaranteed.
This estimate covers the federal stage after nomination. It excludes provincial selection, work permit processing and the required period of business establishment and operation.
Source: IRCC processing times data, accessed 20 October 2026. Federal processing time data.
Contribution Options
No contribution route is described in this summary. These pathways require qualifying business investment and active management.
Government Processing Fees
The applicable fee schedule will be presented at the proposal stage.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified in the supplied summary. All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
Not applicable to this residency summary. These pathways concern permanent residence, rather than the grant of Canadian citizenship or a Canadian passport.
Country Information Sources
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Sources: Parks Canada, accessed 20 October 2026; Statistics Canada, Canada Year Book 2011, accessed 20 October 2026; World Bank Open Data (SP.POP.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD), accessed 22 October 2026; Official Languages Act, preamble, accessed 22 October 2026; Bank of Canada, accessed 22 October 2026.

programmes.cardSummary: A European country offering residence through qualifying real estate and other approved investments.
programmes.overview:
A qualifying investment in real estate or another approved route allows investors to apply for a Greek residence permit. Eligible family members may be included, with a fee of EUR 100 per person.
5–6 months*: Estimated processing time, based on Elevay’s experience.
5 years: Residence permit validity.
From EUR 250,000: Minimum real estate investment, depending on route and area.
Schengen travel: Subject to applicable entry and stay conditions.
Who Can Be Included
Family members can be included for a fee of EUR 100 per person. Your Elevay consultant will confirm who can be included in your case.
Investment Routes
Besides real estate, Greece offers several other investment routes.
[TABLE]
Minimum investment | Investment
EUR 800,000 | Real estate in Attica, Thessaloniki regional unit, Mykonos, Santorini and islands with more than 3,100 people
EUR 400,000 | Real estate everywhere else in Greece
EUR 250,000 | Change of use of a non-residential property, or a listed building restored or reconstructed
EUR 800,000 or EUR 400,000, depending on the area | Tourist accommodation or timeshare
EUR 800,000 | Greek-market listed shares, corporate bonds or Greek government bonds (through a Greek intermediary or bank)
EUR 500,000 | Capital increase shares or bonds of a Greek company listed on a regulated market or a multilateral trading facility (MTF); Capital increase of a Public Limited Real Estate Investment Company (REIC); BPCC/MFBP or Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) / VCC investing only in Greek enterprises; Greek government bonds (at least 3 years remaining); Time deposit in a Greek bank (at least 1 year); Establishing a business
EUR 350,000 | Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) units or shares investing only in Greece
EUR 250,000 | Registered start-up (maximum 33% stake, at least 2 jobs, held 5 years)
[/TABLE]
The residence permit is granted for 5 years and is renewable while the property is not sold.
Each route has its own conditions. Your Elevay consultant will confirm the route that suits your situation and the current requirements before you invest. Fees and requirements may change.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Item | Amount
Government fees, main applicant | EUR 2,016
Family members | EUR 100 per person
Property transfer tax (current) | About 3.09% of the taxable value, paid by the buyer
[/TABLE]
The Greek government has announced an increase of the property transfer tax for non-EU buyers to 15%, planned from 1 July 2027, subject to legislation.
Fees and taxes may change. Please confirm the current figures with your Elevay consultant before you invest.
Sources: stegasi.gov.gr, Greek government housing portal (page modified 4 June 2025; Article 64, Law 5100/2024), accessed 9 October 2026. EUR 250,000 routes, permit duration, government fees and family fee: Elevay management confirmation, 9 October 2026. Transfer tax: AADE (aade.gr, Real Estate Transfer Tax) and Elevay management confirmation. Announced increase: Elevay management confirmation; Greek press reports, September 2026.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.

programmes.name: Hungary Guest Investor Residence
programmes.cardSummary: A European Union and Schengen member state offering residence through qualifying fund investment or donation.
programmes.overview:
The Hungary Guest Investor Residence Permit allows qualifying applicants to reside in Hungary under Act XC of 2023. Applicants may invest in an eligible real estate fund or make a donation to a qualifying higher education institution. The permit does not grant Hungarian or European Union citizenship.
EUR 250,000: Minimum fund investment, held directly and continuously for at least five years.
EUR 1,000,000: Donation to a qualifying higher education institution.
Up to 10 years: Permit validity, extendable once for up to ten more years.
21 days: Statutory administrative period; additional procedural steps are excluded.
Who Can Be Included
Eligible family members can receive a family reunification permit, valid up to 10 years and renewable by up to 10 years. It is linked to the principal permit and cannot outlast it. It also allows work (Art. 73(1)(d)).
Spouse.
The couple’s joint minor children, including adopted and foster children.
The holder’s dependent minor children over whom the holder has parental custody.
The spouse’s dependent minor children over whom the spouse has parental custody.
Adult children and parents are not listed in the Act (Art. 71(2)).
Investment Routes
The applicant chooses one of two routes. Both are set out in the Act.
Option 1 — Real Estate Fund
Invest at least EUR 250,000 in a real estate fund registered by the Hungarian National Bank. Hold the fund share directly and continuously for at least five years.
Fund Route: Conditions In The Act
The fund must have at least 40% of its net assets in Hungarian residential property.
The fund manager must be on the register of qualified market operators (Act XXX of 2016) and meet the asset thresholds set for its type of manager.
The fund share is held in a securities sub-account that is blocked for 5 years.
The certificate of the fund share must be issued in the applicant’s name.
Option 2 — Higher Education Donation
Donate at least EUR 1,000,000 for education, scientific research or artistic creation to a higher education institution maintained by a public-trust foundation with a public-service mission.
The university confirms in a certificate that it received the donation of at least EUR 1,000,000.
When the permit is extended, the donation route does not require a further investment.
Sources: Act XC of 2023 (njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2023-90-00-00), Art. 16(3), 22(9) to (10b) and 22(13); Office for Immigration Factsheet: residence permit for guest investor (oif.gov.hu/factsheets/residence-permit-for-guest-investor); accessed 11 October 2026.
Contribution Options
The EUR 1,000,000 donation route is described under Option 2 above.
Government Processing Fees
The applicable fee schedule will be provided at the proposal stage.
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Programme status: OPEN, checked against the in-force text of the Act on 11 October 2026.
The 21-day period is the official statutory administrative period. It excludes time to submit investment proof, fix deficiencies and complete other procedural steps. It is not a promise of timing. Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved or that a permit will be extended.
Good To Know
The permit allows the holder to run a business or work for others.
Investment changes must be reported within 5 days.
Accommodation in Hungary is required.
How The Application Works
[TABLE]
Step | Detail
Guest investor visa | Valid for 6 months (Art. 16(5)).
Filing the permit application | Inside Hungary, within 30 days of first legal entry, for visa holders and visa-exempt nationals. Online through Enter Hungary, or in person at the regional directorate.
Appearance in person | Required for fingerprints and a photograph, even if the application is filed online.
Proof of investment | Attached within the visa validity, or within 6 months of first entry for visa-exempt nationals (Art. 22(7)).
Changes | Changes to the investment must be reported within 5 days (Art. 22(12)).
Statutory period | 21 days. It excludes time to submit investment proof, fix deficiencies and complete other procedural steps. Not a promise of timing.
Refusal | A refusal can be appealed within 8 days of delivery.
[/TABLE]
Permit Validity And Extension
The permit is valid for up to 10 years and can be extended once, for up to a further 10 years, for the same purpose (Art. 22(6)).
Fund route: the fund share must still be held when the extension is requested.
The extension must be requested at least 30 days before expiry, inside Hungary, through Enter Hungary.
Extension is requested, not automatic.
Work, Business And Presence In Hungary
The holder can run a business or be an executive officer of a company, and can work for others without restriction (Art. 22(1) and (2)).
Under Act XC of 2023 the guest investor permit entitles its holder to stay in Hungary (Art. 22(1)). Conditions: a qualifying investment held for the legal period, accommodation in Hungary, and reporting of changes within 5 days (Art. 22, Art. 17). The Act sets no minimum stay requirement (Art. 22 contains no such rule, and absence from Hungary is not a ground for refusal or withdrawal under Art. 226-227).
Additional Country Information and Sources
European Union (EU) membership: Member since 1 May 2004
Schengen Area membership: Member since 21 December 2007
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Schengen Area
Hungary is part of the Schengen Area, which has 29 countries. Entry and stay conditions are set by each country and can change, so please confirm the current rules with your Elevay consultant.
Austria, France, Liechtenstein, Portugal, Belgium, Germany, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Luxembourg, Slovakia, Croatia, Hungary, Malta, Slovenia, Czechia, Iceland, Netherlands, Spain, Denmark, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Switzerland, Finland.
Sources: European Union, Hungary country page (european-union.europa.eu), accessed 11 October 2026; Schengen list of 29: European Commission, read 9 October 2026.

programmes.name: Latvia Business Residence
programmes.cardSummary: A European Union and Schengen member state offering investor residence through Latvian company share capital.
programmes.overview:
Latvia offers a temporary residence permit through investment in the share capital of a Latvian company. Under the Immigration Law cited in this summary, in force from 15 September 2026, this is the only investor route. Permits are valid for up to two years and may be renewed while the conditions continue to be met.
Up to 2 years: Initial permit validity, renewable while conditions remain satisfied.
EUR 50,000: Share-capital investment in the smaller-company tier.
EUR 100,000: Share-capital investment in the larger-company tier.
EUR 10,000: One-off state payment when requesting the first permit.
EUR 40,000 or EUR 100,000: Annual company tax requirement, depending on tier.
Who Can Be Included
Family members can request a temporary residence permit for the term of the investor’s permit.
The investor’s spouse.
The minor children of the investor or of the spouse, including children under guardianship.
Persons under the investor’s curatorship (aizgādņība).
Family member as defined in Section 1 of the Immigration Law. Your Elevay consultant will confirm who can be included in your case.
Investment Routes
Invest in the share capital of a Latvian company, either in a new company or as an increase of an existing company’s capital. The amount depends on the size of the company (Immigration Law, Art. 27(1)(10)).
[TABLE]
Tier | Company | Investment
Smaller company | Up to 50 employees, and turnover or balance sheet total up to EUR 10 million. Up to 10 foreigners per company on this tier. | EUR 50,000 in share capital
Larger company | More than 50 employees, or turnover or balance sheet total above EUR 10 million (Latvian subsidiaries are counted). | EUR 100,000 in share capital
[/TABLE]
The limit of 10 foreigners per company is stated in the law for the EUR 50,000 tier only.
The Ongoing Condition
[TABLE]
Smaller company | Larger company
EUR 40,000 taxes a year, smaller company. Paid to the state and municipal budgets. | EUR 100,000 taxes a year, larger company. Taxes of Latvian subsidiaries also count.
[/TABLE]
The permit is valid only if, in each reporting year of its validity, the company pays at least this amount in taxes. Refunded taxes are not counted.
Sources: Immigration Law of Latvia, adopted 20 August 2026, in force 15 September 2026 (likumi.lv/ta/id/370622-imigracijas-likums, version valid 15.09.2026–30.12.2027), Art. 27(1)(10)(a) and (b), accessed 20 October 2026. “EUR” is the euro. “EU” is the European Union. “A2” is the second level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Payment | What the law states | Amount
State budget payment | Paid to the state budget when requesting the first permit. One-off and non-refundable, except in cases set by Cabinet regulation (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 30). This is a statutory state payment, not an Elevay fee. | EUR 10,000
[/TABLE]
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Programme status: OPEN, checked against the in-force text of the Act on 11 October 2026.
Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved or renewed.
Good To Know
The permit is valid only while the company keeps paying the required taxes each year.
The EUR 10,000 state payment is non-refundable except in cases set by Cabinet regulation.
State Payment And The Permit
The state budget payment is paid to the state budget when requesting the first permit. It is one-off and non-refundable, except in cases set by Cabinet regulation (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 30). This is a statutory state payment, not an Elevay fee.
[TABLE]
Stage | What the law states
First permit | Temporary residence permit for up to 2 years (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 29(3)).
Each reporting year | The company pays the required taxes (EUR 40,000, or EUR 100,000 for the larger tier).
Renewal | Available while the conditions still exist. It is never guaranteed.
[/TABLE]
Permanent Residence
As of 20 October 2026, the only permanent residence in Latvia is European Union (EU) long-term resident status. The law requires 5 years of continuous residence, sufficient means, Latvian at A2 level and a Latvian culture and history course. Permanent residence is never guaranteed.
The current version of the law is valid until 30 December 2027, so this wording may change.
Sources: Immigration Law of Latvia, adopted 20 August 2026, in force 15 September 2026 (likumi.lv/ta/id/370622-imigracijas-likums, version valid 15.09.2026–30.12.2027), Sections 1, 27, 29 and 30; Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs, article “New Immigration Law takes effect: key changes and regulations”, 15 September 2026 (pmlp.gov.lv/en/article/new-immigration-law-takes-effect-key-changes-and-regulations). Read 20 October 2026. “EUR” is the euro. “EU” is the European Union. “A2” is the second level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
Additional Country Information and Sources
EU membership: Member since 1 May 2004

Program Overview
Latvia offers a temporary residence permit through investment in the share capital of a Latvian company. Under the Immigration Law cited in this summary, in force from 15 September 2026, this is the only investor route. Permits are valid for up to two years and may be renewed while the conditions continue to be met.
Up to 2 years: Initial permit validity, renewable while conditions remain satisfied.
EUR 50,000: Share-capital investment in the smaller-company tier.
EUR 100,000: Share-capital investment in the larger-company tier.
EUR 10,000: One-off state payment when requesting the first permit.
EUR 40,000 or EUR 100,000: Annual company tax requirement, depending on tier.
Who Can Be Included
Family members can request a temporary residence permit for the term of the investor’s permit.
The investor’s spouse.
The minor children of the investor or of the spouse, including children under guardianship.
Persons under the investor’s curatorship (aizgādņība).
Family member as defined in Section 1 of the Immigration Law. Your Elevay consultant will confirm who can be included in your case.
Investment Routes
Invest in the share capital of a Latvian company, either in a new company or as an increase of an existing company’s capital. The amount depends on the size of the company (Immigration Law, Art. 27(1)(10)).
[TABLE]
Tier | Company | Investment
Smaller company | Up to 50 employees, and turnover or balance sheet total up to EUR 10 million. Up to 10 foreigners per company on this tier. | EUR 50,000 in share capital
Larger company | More than 50 employees, or turnover or balance sheet total above EUR 10 million (Latvian subsidiaries are counted). | EUR 100,000 in share capital
[/TABLE]
The limit of 10 foreigners per company is stated in the law for the EUR 50,000 tier only.
The Ongoing Condition
[TABLE]
Smaller company | Larger company
EUR 40,000 taxes a year, smaller company. Paid to the state and municipal budgets. | EUR 100,000 taxes a year, larger company. Taxes of Latvian subsidiaries also count.
[/TABLE]
The permit is valid only if, in each reporting year of its validity, the company pays at least this amount in taxes. Refunded taxes are not counted.
Sources: Immigration Law of Latvia, adopted 20 August 2026, in force 15 September 2026 (likumi.lv/ta/id/370622-imigracijas-likums, version valid 15.09.2026–30.12.2027), Art. 27(1)(10)(a) and (b), accessed 20 October 2026. “EUR” is the euro. “EU” is the European Union. “A2” is the second level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Payment | What the law states | Amount
State budget payment | Paid to the state budget when requesting the first permit. One-off and non-refundable, except in cases set by Cabinet regulation (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 30). This is a statutory state payment, not an Elevay fee. | EUR 10,000
[/TABLE]
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Programme status: OPEN, checked against the in-force text of the Act on 11 October 2026.
Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved or renewed.
Good To Know
The permit is valid only while the company keeps paying the required taxes each year.
The EUR 10,000 state payment is non-refundable except in cases set by Cabinet regulation.
State Payment And The Permit
The state budget payment is paid to the state budget when requesting the first permit. It is one-off and non-refundable, except in cases set by Cabinet regulation (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 30). This is a statutory state payment, not an Elevay fee.
[TABLE]
Stage | What the law states
First permit | Temporary residence permit for up to 2 years (Art. 27(1)(10) and Art. 29(3)).
Each reporting year | The company pays the required taxes (EUR 40,000, or EUR 100,000 for the larger tier).
Renewal | Available while the conditions still exist. It is never guaranteed.
[/TABLE]
Permanent Residence
As of 20 October 2026, the only permanent residence in Latvia is European Union (EU) long-term resident status. The law requires 5 years of continuous residence, sufficient means, Latvian at A2 level and a Latvian culture and history course. Permanent residence is never guaranteed.
The current version of the law is valid until 30 December 2027, so this wording may change.

Read 20 October 2026. “EUR” is the euro. “EU” is the European Union. “A2” is the second level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

Latvia has been part of the Schengen Area since 21 December 2007. The Schengen Area has 29 countries. Entry and stay conditions are set by each country and can change, so please confirm the current rules with your Elevay consultant.

programmes.overview:
The Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP) allows eligible non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss nationals to apply for permanent residence. Applicants rent or buy a qualifying home, make the required government payments and demonstrate sufficient capital assets. Residency Malta administers the programme. It provides permanent residence in Malta and Schengen travel for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; it does not itself grant citizenship.
6–9 months: Typical processing time, based on Elevay’s experience; no official processing time is published.
Permanent residence: Subject to continuing compliance with programme conditions.
5 years: Minimum qualifying property and capital-asset period.
No minimum annual stay: The MPRP regulations specify no minimum number of days.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse or partner in a relationship similar to marriage.
Children under 18.
Children aged 18 to 28 who are unmarried and mainly dependent on the main applicant.
Parents or grandparents of the applicant or spouse who are not in full-time employment and are mainly dependent on the applicant.
Adult children with a certified disability.
The Agency brochure says an application may include up to four generations.
Applicant Eligibility
Non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss nationals, not from countries the Agency lists as sanctioned.
Stable and regular resources enough to support the applicant and dependants without Malta’s social assistance.
A clean criminal record, and no threat to national security, public policy, public health or public interest.
Every application goes through multi-tier due diligence. Approval is never guaranteed.
Investment Routes
The main applicant meets the property requirement in one of two ways, rent or buy, and keeps the capital for 5 years.
Option 1 — Rent a Qualifying Home
Rent a residential property in Malta or Gozo for at least EUR 14,000 a year, and hold the lease as your residence for at least 5 years.
Option 2 — Buy a Qualifying Home
Buy a residential property in Malta or Gozo worth at least EUR 375,000, and hold it as your residence for at least 5 years.
Either way, the property must be held as the residence for a minimum of 5 years. After 5 years, the beneficiary must still hold a residential property in Malta or Gozo, owned or leased. With the Agency’s consent the property can be replaced with another qualifying one. A property bought for less than EUR 375,000 counts if works paid by the main applicant bring its value to at least EUR 375,000. The Agency may carry out spot checks of the property.
Capital Assets
[TABLE]
Option | Capital assets | Of which financial assets
Option 1 | at least EUR 500,000 | EUR 150,000
Option 2 | at least EUR 650,000 | EUR 75,000
[/TABLE]
The capital must be kept for 5 years. The Agency decides in its sole discretion which assets count as financial assets.
Required Government Contribution and Donation
A EUR 37,000 government contribution and EUR 2,000 donation are required, in addition to the property and capital-asset conditions. See the fee schedule below.
Government Processing Fees
Government Fees And Payment Timing
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount | Who pays and when
Administration fee, non-refundable | EUR 60,000 | Main applicant, in two instalments: EUR 15,000 within 1 month of submitting the application and EUR 45,000 within 2 months of the Letter of Approval in Principle.
Government contribution | EUR 37,000 | Main applicant, within 8 months of the Approval in Principle. The same amount for owned or rented property.
Dependant administration fee | EUR 7,500 each | For children aged 18 to 28, and for parents and grandparents. No fee for the spouse or partner, children under 18, or adult children with a certified disability.
Donation | EUR 2,000 | Main applicant, to a registered local non-governmental organisation (NGO).
Residence card | EUR 500 per person | Each person; covers 5 years. Agency brochure figure; not printed in the law.
[/TABLE]
Also required: health insurance covering all risks normally covered for Maltese nationals. Government fees can vary. Property purchase or rental costs and professional fees are separate and are not included here.
Payment Timeline
[TABLE]
When | Payment
Within 1 month of submitting the application | EUR 15,000 first instalment of the administration fee
Within 2 months of the Letter of Approval in Principle | EUR 45,000 second instalment of the administration fee
Within 8 months of the Approval in Principle | EUR 37,000 government contribution
[/TABLE]
No total is shown. The Agency does not publish a total, and the final cost depends on the number of dependants and on the property. Your Elevay consultant will prepare a personal cost estimate.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
Visa-free travel across the Schengen Area for 90 days in any 180-day period.
Residence and Application Details
Processing takes about 6 to 9 months based on Elevay’s experience. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline; the Agency publishes no processing time. The Agency says decisions are communicated within a reasonable timeframe and that processing starts when a complete and correct file is submitted.
A temporary residence permit valid for 1 year can be applied for when the application is submitted, for the applicant and dependants.
The MPRP regulations set no minimum number of days a year in Malta. Hold a qualifying home as your residence for at least 5 years. After that, hold a residential property in Malta or Gozo, owned or leased. Keep the capital assets for 5 years, and keep the required health insurance. Your permanent residence can be withdrawn if you stop meeting the conditions (for example, you no longer hold the property or keep the capital), if false information was given in the application, or if the authorities decide that your stay is against the public interest.
The MPRP does not give citizenship by itself, and buying or renting a property under it gives no right to citizenship. A beneficiary who actually lives in Malta may apply for Maltese citizenship by naturalisation under the general citizenship law, like any other foreign resident. The law asks for residence in Malta throughout the 12 months before applying and for at least 4 years in the 6 years before that, adequate knowledge of Maltese or English, good character and suitability. The Minister decides each case, so approval is never guaranteed. If the beneficiary becomes a Maltese national, the MPRP certificate ceases.
Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved.
Additional Country Information and Sources
European Union (EU) membership: Member since 1 May 2004
Schengen Area membership: Member since 21 December 2007
GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Schengen Area
Malta is part of the Schengen Area, which has 29 countries. Entry and stay conditions are set by each country and can change, so please confirm the current rules with your Elevay consultant.
Austria, France, Liechtenstein, Portugal, Belgium, Germany, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Luxembourg, Slovakia, Croatia, Hungary, Malta, Slovenia, Czechia, Iceland, Netherlands, Spain, Denmark, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Switzerland, Finland.
Sources: S.L. 217.26 as amended by LN 310/2024 and LN 146/2025 (Residency Malta regulations); Residency Malta legal framework; Residency Malta MPRP brochure; Maltese Citizenship Act, Cap. 188 (legislation.mt/eli/cap/188/eng); Agenzija Komunita Malta, acquisition of citizenship (komunita.gov.mt/services/acquisition-of-citizenship). Accessed 10 and 13 October 2026.

programmes.overview:
The Malta Nomad Residence Permit allows eligible non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss nationals aged 18 or over to live in Malta while working remotely for an employer, business or clients abroad. Residency Malta administers the programme. The initial permit is valid for one year.
About 30 working days: Agency expectation from receipt of payment, excluding visa processing.
1 year: Initial permit validity.
Up to 4 years: Maximum total stay through three discretionary renewals.
EUR 42,000: Minimum gross annual income, guaranteed for at least five months from application.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse.
Minor children.
Unmarried adult children who are mainly dependent on the applicant.
Adult children unable to cope independently because of a medical condition or disability.
Dependants are added at application or at renewal; newborns are the exception.
Eligibility and Remote Work
Option 1 — Employee
Employed by an employer registered abroad, with an employment contract.
Option 2 — Business owner
Running, or being a partner or shareholder in, a business for a company registered abroad.
Option 3 — Freelancer or consultant
Working for clients with a permanent establishment abroad, with contracts.
Minimum gross income: EUR 42,000 a year, guaranteed for at least 5 months from the application date.
A valid travel document is required.
A property rental or purchase agreement covering the permit period.
Health insurance covering the EU (including Malta) and the UK, as the Agency requires, with minimum cover of EUR 100,000. It must be pre-paid for 1 full year; travel insurance is not accepted.
A police conduct certificate and a background check.
Not eligible:
People contracted by a foreign company to serve its Maltese subsidiary, or serving Malta-based companies or individuals.
Nationals of, or people with close ties to, Afghanistan, North Korea, Iran, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Yemen and Venezuela. Applications from the Russian Federation and Belarus are currently not eligible either. The Agency may revise this list.
Your Elevay consultant confirms which family members can be included and prepares the document list (see the separate Document Checklist).
Sources: Nomad Residence Permit eligibility page and FAQ v14.1, last updated 17 April 2026. Accessed 10 and 13 October 2026.
