Program Overview
The Malta Nomad Residence Permit allows eligible non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss nationals aged 18 or over to live in Malta while working remotely for an employer, business or clients abroad. Residency Malta administers the programme. The initial permit is valid for one year.
About 30 working days: Agency expectation from receipt of payment, excluding visa processing.
1 year: Initial permit validity.
Up to 4 years: Maximum total stay through three discretionary renewals.
EUR 42,000: Minimum gross annual income, guaranteed for at least five months from application.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse.
Minor children.
Unmarried adult children who are mainly dependent on the applicant.
Adult children unable to cope independently because of a medical condition or disability.
Dependants are added at application or at renewal; newborns are the exception.
Eligibility and Remote Work
Option 1 — Employee
Employed by an employer registered abroad, with an employment contract.
Option 2 — Business owner
Running, or being a partner or shareholder in, a business for a company registered abroad.
Option 3 — Freelancer or consultant
Working for clients with a permanent establishment abroad, with contracts.
Minimum gross income: EUR 42,000 a year, guaranteed for at least 5 months from the application date.
A valid travel document is required.
A property rental or purchase agreement covering the permit period.
Health insurance covering the EU (including Malta) and the UK, as the Agency requires, with minimum cover of EUR 100,000. It must be pre-paid for 1 full year; travel insurance is not accepted.
A police conduct certificate and a background check.
Not eligible:
People contracted by a foreign company to serve its Maltese subsidiary, or serving Malta-based companies or individuals.
Nationals of, or people with close ties to, Afghanistan, North Korea, Iran, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Yemen and Venezuela. Applications from the Russian Federation and Belarus are currently not eligible either. The Agency may revise this list.
Your Elevay consultant confirms which family members can be included and prepares the document list (see the separate Document Checklist).

programmes.cardSummary: A European Union and Schengen member state with residence programmes for investors, remote workers and eligible tax residents.
programmes.overview:
Malta’s tax residence programmes apply a 15% tax rate to foreign income received in Malta, subject to an annual minimum tax and a qualifying home. The applicable programme depends on nationality and circumstances: the Global Residence Programme, the Residence Programme or the Malta Retirement Programme. The separate changes scheduled for 1 January 2027 are set out below.
15%: Tax on foreign income received in Malta.
EUR 15,000: Annual minimum for the Global Residence and Residence Programmes under the earlier rules.
EUR 7,500: Retirement Programme annual minimum, plus EUR 500 for each dependant and special carer.
1 January 2027: Separate new rules and transition provisions apply.
Who Can Be Included
Family treatment depends on the selected tax programme. The Global Residence and Residence Programme minimums cover the beneficiary, spouse and certain children; the Retirement Programme adds an annual amount for each dependant and special carer. Confirm eligibility for each family member before applying.
Programme Eligibility
Categories from 1 January 2027
Categories: Global resident; EU, EEA and Swiss resident; retired pensioner; United Nations (UN) pensioner. The full eligibility conditions for each 2027 category are not covered here. This summary will be updated in January 2027.
Earlier Programme Conditions
Global Residence and Residence Programme applicants must communicate adequately in Maltese or English. A qualifying property must be bought or rented and used as the primary residence. The Retirement Programme language position is shown separately below.
[TABLE]
Condition | Global Residence Programme | Residence Programme | Malta Retirement Programme
Nationality | Not Maltese, EEA or Swiss: a third-country national | EU, EEA or Swiss national, not Maltese | Any nationality except Maltese
Income | Stable and regular resources to support the beneficiary and dependants without social assistance | Stable and regular resources to support the beneficiary and dependants without social assistance | A pension, documented and received in Malta, that is at least 75% of chargeable income
Insurance | Sickness insurance for all risks across the whole European Union, for the beneficiary and dependants | Sickness insurance for all risks across the whole European Union, for the beneficiary and dependants | Sickness insurance for all risks across the whole European Union, for the beneficiary and dependants
Language | Can adequately communicate in one of Malta’s official languages (Maltese or English) | Can adequately communicate in one of Malta’s official languages (Maltese or English) | No language condition in the rules
Other | Fit and proper person; valid travel document; not a permanent or long-term resident of Malta; not already under another listed Maltese scheme | Fit and proper person; valid travel document; not a permanent or long-term resident of Malta; not already under another listed Maltese scheme | Fit and proper person; valid travel document; not domiciled in Malta and no intention to become domiciled within 5 years of applying; not under another listed scheme
Days in Malta | No minimum number of days is set | No minimum number of days is set | At least 90 days a year, averaged over any 5-year period
[/TABLE]
No more than 183 days in any other country in a calendar year.
When Tax Status Ends
The beneficiary becomes a Maltese national, or a permanent or long-term resident of Malta.
The qualifying property is lost, including by letting or subletting it, or the required insurance lapses.
The 183-day limit is passed, or (Malta Retirement Programme) the 90-day average is not met.
The authorities decide the stay is against the public interest, or the tax laws are breached.
Sources: S.L. 123.148, S.L. 123.160 and S.L. 123.134, rules 2, 4 and 6 (legislation.mt); official languages: European Union, Malta country page (europa.eu); accessed 10 and 13 October 2026. Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved.
Investment Routes
[TABLE]
Programme | Property requirement
Global Residence Programme and Residence Programme | Buy for at least EUR 275,000 in Malta or EUR 220,000 in Gozo or the south of Malta; or rent for at least EUR 9,600 a year in Malta or EUR 8,750 in Gozo or the south. It must be the primary residence.
Malta Retirement Programme | Buy for at least EUR 275,000 in Malta or EUR 220,000 in Gozo or the south of Malta; or rent for at least EUR 9,600 a year in Malta or EUR 8,750 in Gozo or the south. It must be the primary residence.
[/TABLE]
From 1 January 2027: Buy for at least EUR 700,000, or rent for at least EUR 14,000 a year.
Sources: Global Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.148; Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.160; Malta Retirement Programme Rules, S.L. 123.134; Individual Tax Programme Rules 2026, LN 195/2026, accessed 10 and 13 October 2026.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Programme | Administration fee
Global Residence Programme | EUR 6,000 (EUR 5,500 where the property is owned in the south of Malta)
Residence Programme | EUR 6,000 (EUR 5,500 where the property is owned in the south of Malta)
Malta Retirement Programme | EUR 2,500
[/TABLE]
Fees are non-refundable. Applications are made through an authorised registered mandatary. Government fees can vary.
From 1 January 2027: Administration fee EUR 8,500, non-refundable.
Sources: Global Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.148 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.148/eng); Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.160 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.160/eng); Malta Retirement Programme Rules, S.L. 123.134 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.134/eng); Individual Tax Programme Rules 2026, LN 195/2026 (legislation.mt/eli/ln/2026/195/eng); accessed 10 and 13 October 2026.

No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Changes from 1 January 2027
The Individual Tax Programme Rules 2026 (LN 195/2026, Gazette 14 July 2026) apply from 1 January 2027.
[TABLE]
Item | Detail
Tax | 15% on income arising outside Malta and received in Malta
Minimum tax a year | EUR 35,000 for global resident and EU, EEA and Swiss resident status; EUR 15,000 for retired pensioner status
Status | 5 years, renewable for further 5-year periods
Earlier status | Status granted, or applications received, up to 31 December 2026 continue under the earlier rules until 31 December 2031
[/TABLE]
Tax Rules Before 1 January 2027
Minimum tax is the least amount payable each year, whatever the income received in Malta. No processing time is published, so none is shown. Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved.
15% rate. Income arising outside Malta that is received in Malta in the previous year is taxed at 15%.
Minimum tax. Whatever the amount received in Malta, the tax payable for the year is at least the minimum: EUR 15,000 under the Global Residence and Residence Programmes (for the beneficiary, spouse and certain children), or EUR 7,500 under the Malta Retirement Programme, plus EUR 500 a year for each dependant and special carer.
So the minimum is a floor, not a cap. The 15% is never limited to EUR 15,000. Once 15% of the income received in Malta is more than the minimum, the tax is the 15% amount.
The minimum is payable in full in the year status is granted and in the year it ends, and tax paid under the rules is not refundable.
Income that is not taxed at 15% under these rules is taxed separately at 35%.
[TABLE]
Income received in Malta in the year | 15% of that income | Tax payable (Global Residence or Residence Programme)
EUR 40,000 | EUR 6,000 | EUR 15,000 (the minimum)
EUR 100,000 | EUR 15,000 | EUR 15,000
EUR 200,000 | EUR 30,000 | EUR 30,000 (the 15% amount)
[/TABLE]
The 15% amount passes the EUR 15,000 minimum at EUR 100,000 of income received in Malta (EUR 50,000 for the Malta Retirement Programme minimum of EUR 7,500). This is simple arithmetic of the rule, not a tax calculation, and double taxation relief may apply.
The tax position depends on personal circumstances. Independent tax advice is recommended. Elevay does not give tax advice. This summary makes no tax calculation for any individual.
Sources: Global Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.148 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.148/eng); Residence Programme Rules, S.L. 123.160 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.160/eng); Malta Retirement Programme Rules, S.L. 123.134 (legislation.mt/eli/sl/123.134/eng); Individual Tax Programme Rules 2026, LN 195/2026 (legislation.mt/eli/ln/2026/195/eng). Accessed 10 and 13 October 2026.

programmes.overview:
The Portugal D2 Residence Visa is for applicants who intend to work independently or operate a business in Portugal. Elevay covers three routes: independent professional, immigrant entrepreneur and Startup Visa. Following the visa stage, the Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum (AIMA) issues the temporary residence permit.
3–6 months*: Estimated processing time, based on Elevay’s experience.
2 years: Initial residence permit, renewable in three-year periods.
6 consecutive months or 8 months in total: Unjustified absence limits during the two-year permit.
EUR 6,440: Indicative means for one adult; Elevay’s seven-month calculation, not an official published threshold.
* Based on Elevay’s experience. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse
Minor or dependent children, and adopted minors
Unmarried adult children who are studying
Dependent first-degree parents of the main applicant or of the spouse
Minor siblings under guardianship
The Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum (AIMA) assesses dependency and study conditions.
Family members: Law No. 23/2007, Art. 99 (diariodarepublica.pt); Elevay management confirmation, 10 October 2026, that the same family rules apply to all Portugal programmes.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Independent professional — Art. 60(1)
For people who will work for themselves in Portugal, such as consultants and freelancers. The applicant must show a services contract or a written proposal to provide services, plus the right to practise where the profession requires it.
Option 2 — Immigrant entrepreneur — Art. 60(2)
For people who invest in or set up a business in Portugal. Portuguese law sets no minimum investment amount for this route. The applicant must show investment operations already made, or financial means available in Portugal (including financing from a Portuguese financial institution), plus proof by any means of the intention to invest.
Option 3 — Startup Visa — Art. 89(4)
For founders whose project is accepted by a certified incubator in Portugal. A declaration from the Agency for Competitiveness and Innovation (IAPMEI) certifies the incubation contract.
Indicative Funds to Show
The law asks for means of subsistence for a period not less than the maximum admissible stay. We read that as the 4-month residence visa plus a 90-day extension, which is about 7 months. We multiply 7 months by the 2026 minimum wage of EUR 920 a month, with the official shares: first adult 100%, second adult 50%, each child 30%.
[TABLE]
Household | Calculation | Indicative amount
One adult | 7 x EUR 920 | EUR 6,440
Second adult (spouse), added | 50% of EUR 6,440 | EUR 3,220
Each child, added | 30% of EUR 6,440 | EUR 1,932
Couple | 6,440 + 3,220 | EUR 9,660
Couple plus one child | 9,660 + 1,932 | EUR 11,592
[/TABLE]
Indicative only. The 7-month period is our reading of the law, and these amounts are not an official published figure. Please confirm with the consulate. Meeting them does not guarantee that a visa will be granted.
Sources: Law No. 23/2007, Arts. 58(2), 60, 72(1)(c) and 89(4) (diariodarepublica.pt); Portaria No. 1563/2007, Art. 5; vistos.mne.gov.pt/en/national-visas/necessary-documentation/residency; minimum wage: dgert.gov.pt; accessed 10 October 2026.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
National visa fee | EUR 110
Residence permit: issue or renewal | EUR 114.30
Permanent residence permit | EUR 351.10
[/TABLE]
AIMA table in force from 1 March 2026. Standard rates in euros (EUR). Government fees can vary.
Sources: AIMA fee table (Portaria No. 307/2023), in force from 1 March 2026 (aima.gov.pt), standard rates; national visa fee: vistos.mne.gov.pt/en/national-visas/general-information/fees; accessed 10 October 2026. Processing time: Elevay management confirmation, 10 October 2026.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Citizenship Eligibility
Under Organic Law No. 1/2026, in force from 19 May 2026, Portuguese nationality by residence requires 10 years of legal residence, or 7 years for nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries and of European Union (EU) member states. Citizenship is never guaranteed or automatic, and other conditions apply. Applications filed before 19 May 2026 keep the earlier law.
Sources: Organic Law No. 1/2026 (justica.gov.pt, Nationality Law news item). Accessed 10 October 2026 unless stated.
Residence and Application Details
The residence permit can be cancelled if you are absent from Portugal for more than 6 consecutive months, or 8 months in total, during its 2-year validity, without justified reason. In practice, plan to spend around 16 of the 24 months in Portugal.
[TABLE]
Period | Detail
6 months in a row | The longest unjustified absence
8 months in total | Unjustified absence within the 2 years
16 of 24 months | A planning guide, not a legal minimum
[/TABLE]
The law sets no minimum number of days. The 16-month figure is a planning guide calculated from the legal limits. Cancellation is possible, not automatic. Absences beyond these limits must be justified to the Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum (AIMA) before you leave. The law provides that the permit is not cancelled if the holder was carrying out professional, business, cultural or social activity while away. For a permanent residence permit, the limits are 24 consecutive months or 30 months in total within three years.
[TABLE]
Visa and permit item | Detail
Visa | Valid for two entries and 4 months. Legal decision deadline: 60 days (Law No. 23/2007, Art. 58).
Residence permit | Valid for 2 years, renewable in successive 3-year periods (Art. 75(1)).
Renewal conditions | Means of subsistence, accommodation, tax and social security obligations met, and no conviction above 1 year (Art. 78(2)). Renewal is never guaranteed.
[/TABLE]
Sources: Law No. 23/2007, Arts. 58, 60, 72, 75, 78 and 85, consolidated text including Law No. 62/2026, in force 11 September 2026 (diariodarepublica.pt); vistos.mne.gov.pt (residency documentation); Portaria No. 1563/2007, Art. 5; accessed 10 October 2026. programmes.name: Portugal Golden Visa
programmes.cardSummary: A European Union and Schengen member state offering residence pathways for entrepreneurs, income holders, remote workers and investors.
programmes.overview:
The Portugal Golden Visa is a residence authorisation for investment activity under Article 90-A of Law No. 23/2007. A qualifying investment maintained for at least five years allows the investor and eligible family members to apply for a Portuguese residence permit.
About 24 months*: Processing time, based on current Elevay cases.
7 days per year†: Minimum stay stated by Elevay management.
5 years: Minimum period for maintaining the investment.
From EUR 200,000: Cultural investment in a qualifying low-density territory. The job-creation route has no specified investment amount.
* Based on Elevay’s current cases. AIMA is working to reduce processing times. This is not an official or guaranteed timeline.
† Minimum stay: Elevay management confirmation.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse
Minor or dependent children, and adopted minors
Unmarried adult children who are studying
Dependent first-degree parents of the main applicant or of the spouse
Minor siblings under guardianship
AIMA assesses dependency and study conditions. Eligibility is assessed individually.
Investment Routes
The six routes listed below require the qualifying investment to be maintained for at least five years.
Option 1 — Job Creation
Create at least ten jobs. No minimum investment amount is specified.
Option 2 — Scientific Research
Transfer at least EUR 500,000 into scientific research institutions.
Option 3 — Culture
Transfer at least EUR 250,000 into artistic production or the recovery or maintenance of national cultural heritage through qualifying public or public-interest bodies.
Option 4 — Venture Capital or Company-Capitalisation Funds
Invest at least EUR 500,000 in fund units with a maturity of at least five years and at least 60% invested in companies based in Portugal.
Option 5 — Collective Investment Undertakings
Invest at least EUR 500,000 in non-real-estate fund units with a maturity of at least five years and at least 60% invested in companies based in Portugal.
Option 6 — Company Establishment or Capital Increase
Invest at least EUR 500,000 to establish a Portuguese company with five permanent jobs, or increase company capital with five permanent jobs, or maintain ten jobs, including at least five permanent positions, for three years.
Low-Density Territories
Under Portaria No. 208/2017, the minimum may be reduced by 20% for the following routes in qualifying low-density territories. The fund routes receive no reduction.
[TABLE]
Route | Low-density minimum
Job creation | 8 jobs
Scientific research | EUR 400,000
Culture | EUR 200,000
[/TABLE]
Government Processing Fees
AIMA standard rates, in force from 1 March 2026. Amounts may change.
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Receipt and analysis of application | EUR 842.80
Grant of investor residence permit | EUR 8,418.90
Grant for each family member | EUR 8,418.90 per person
Renewal of investor residence permit | EUR 4,210.30
Renewal for each family member | EUR 4,210.30 per person
[/TABLE]
Permanent Residence Fees
[TABLE]
Fee | Amount
Grant of permanent residence — holder or family member | EUR 11,786.70
Renewal of permanent residence | EUR 5,894.10
[/TABLE]
Legal, fund or company establishment and tax advice costs depend on the chosen route.
Residence and Renewal
Maintain the investment for at least five years. The permit is renewed in two-year periods while the investment requirement continues to be met. The minimum stay stated by Elevay management is seven days per year.
Permanent Residence
Article 80 of Law No. 23/2007 requires five years of temporary residence, basic Portuguese, means of subsistence and housing. Permanent residence is not guaranteed.
Travel Access
Portugal is part of the Schengen Area, which has 29 countries. Entry and stay conditions are set by each country and may change. Confirm the current rules before travel.
Austria, France, Liechtenstein, Portugal, Belgium, Germany, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Luxembourg, Slovakia, Croatia, Hungary, Malta, Slovenia, Czechia, Iceland, Netherlands, Spain, Denmark, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Switzerland, Finland.
Sources
Portuguese Law No. 23/2007, consolidated text, Diário da República; AIMA fee notice, accessed 10 October 2026. Processing time and minimum stay: Elevay management confirmation.
Country facts: World Bank Open Data, Constitution of Portugal and European Union country information, as listed in the Portugal sections.
Family Scope of Figures
Each investment, contribution, income or fee figure applies only to the applicant or family composition stated beside that figure. If no family size is stated, the programme information does not specify one.

programmes.overview:
Spain’s Digital Nomad Visa and residence authorisation allow eligible adult non-EU nationals to live in Spain while working remotely for companies abroad, using information technology and telecommunications. The programme operates under Articles 74 bis to 74 quinquies of Law 14/2013. Applicants may apply through a Spanish consulate or, when lawfully in Spain, through the Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit (UGE).
Up to 20 days: Legal maximum for the residence authorisation after electronic filing; not a guaranteed overall timeline.
Up to 1 year: Consular teleworking visa validity.
Up to 3 years: Residence authorisation, renewable in two-year periods.
EUR 34,188: Main applicant’s gross annual income requirement, calculated from the cited 2026 minimum wage.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse or partner in an analogous relationship.
An unmarried, unregistered partner shows at least 1 year of continuous cohabitation, unless there are common children.
Minor children.
Adult children who depend economically on the holder and have not formed their own family unit: aged 18 to under 26 if they meet the UGE conditions, and 26 or over only with an incapacity.
Aged 18 to under 26: no income from work or public benefits, and enrolled in a qualifying course or registered as a job-seeker. Aged 26 or over: only with an incapacity that prevents them from being economically independent.
Dependent parents and grandparents. Dependent ascendants show economic or physical dependence; over 80 is presumed.
Family members may apply with the holder or later, and may work in Spain without restriction, as employees or self-employed.
Applicant Eligibility
Adult third-country nationals only. Citizens of the EU and people covered by EU law are excluded. Holders of a non-lucrative residence permit cannot apply on that permit, because it does not allow work.
Remote Work Conditions
Remote work for companies located outside Spain, using exclusively information technology and telecommunication means. An employee may work only for companies outside Spain. A professional (self-employed) may also serve a Spanish company for up to 20% of their total professional activity (Article 74 bis).
Qualifications
A degree or postgraduate qualification from a recognised university, vocational school or business school, or at least 3 years of professional experience (Article 74 bis).
Foreign Company Requirements
The company or group must show real, continuous activity for at least 1 year (Article 74 ter).
Working Relationship
The employment or professional relationship with the company outside Spain must have lasted at least the last 3 months before applying, with documents showing that remote work is allowed or the terms of the remote activity. This proof is not asked of someone who already holds a teleworker visa or an earlier initial authorisation.
General Conditions
Over 18, no criminal record, health insurance, sufficient resources and the fee paid (Article 62.3).
Income Requirements
[TABLE]
Who | Gross annual income required
Main applicant | 200% of the minimum wage. The annual 2026 minimum wage is EUR 17,094 (Royal Decree 126/2026, Article 3, in force from 20 February 2026), so 200% is EUR 34,188 a year (gross).
Family unit of two | The holder plus one family member: at least 75% of the annual minimum wage for the family member: EUR 12,820.50 a year (gross).
Each further member | 25% of the annual minimum wage for each further family member: EUR 4,273.50 a year each (gross).
[/TABLE]
Amounts are gross, before tax and Social Security. The UGE states the requirement as a percentage of the minimum wage and does not print a euro total; the annual figures are Elevay’s calculation from the 2026 minimum wage in Royal Decree 126/2026. “UGE” is the Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit of the Spanish Inclusion Ministry (Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos).
Sources: Law 14/2013, consolidated text, Official State Gazette (BOE), Articles 62, 74 bis and 74 ter; Royal Decree 126/2026 on the 2026 minimum wage (BOE); UGE holder guide v2 (holder guide); UGE frequently asked questions in English (FAQs). Accessed 22 October 2026.

Investment Routes
No qualifying investment is required under this route.
Social Security Contributions
Social Security Registration
Self-employed holders must register with the self-employed Social Security scheme (RETA) as soon as the authorisation is granted and before starting work in Spain. Late registration can end the authorisation, and the holder and dependants can then be barred from living and working in Spain. Do not wait. Employees register with the General Regime, or show a certificate that home-country cover applies.
Reduced RETA Contributions
Tarifa plana is a reduced monthly quota for new self-employed workers: from about EUR 88.56 a month for the first 12 months. A further 12 months is possible only if net annual income is below the annual minimum wage. It must be requested when you register, and is not available if you were registered in RETA in the previous 2 years. After the reduced period you pay an income-based quota, which depends on your net income.
Check Current Contributions
The Spanish Social Security administration publishes the current contribution tables and a simulator. Please check them here: seg-social.es, “Nuevo sistema de cotización para autónomos”. The quota is the Social Security cost only; it excludes tax and any adviser costs.
Sources: Law 14/2013, Arts. 62.4, 62.5 (BOE); UGE family and holder guides v2, FAQs (inclusion.gob.es); Seguridad Social (seg-social.es); RDL 13/2022. Accessed 22 October 2026. Contribution information: Social Security administration, not the UGE. Tarifa plana of about EUR 88.56: Elevay figure, to be confirmed on an official page.
Government Processing Fees
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Up to 20 days: Legal maximum for the residence authorisation, from electronic filing. This is a legal maximum, not a promise. Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved.
Route 1: Up to 1 year. Teleworking visa issued by a Spanish consulate.
Route 2: Up to 3 years. Residence authorisation, renewable in 2-year periods while conditions are met.
The two routes are separate paths. Each has its own validity. The periods are not added together, because the law gives each one separately and does not state how they combine.
Option 1 — Apply from Abroad
For non-residents who plan to live in Spain and telework for a company outside Spain. They apply for the international teleworking visa. Visas are issued by Spanish diplomatic missions and consulates. The visa is valid for a maximum of 1 year, or for the same period as the work if that is shorter. While valid, it is sufficient title to live and work remotely in Spain. Within the 60 calendar days before the visa expires, the holder may apply for the residence authorisation if the conditions still hold.
Option 2 — Apply from Inside Spain
For people already lawfully in Spain, or who entered on the teleworker visa. They apply for the residence authorisation with the UGE. The authorisation is valid for the time requested, up to a maximum of 3 years. It can be renewed in 2-year periods while the conditions that gave the right still hold. If the authorisation lasts more than 6 months, the holder must then apply for the foreigner identity card.
The UGE handles the residence authorisation electronically. The law sets a maximum of 20 days from electronic filing. If no decision is made in that time, the authorisation is deemed granted by administrative silence (Article 76.1).
Sources: Law 14/2013, consolidated text, Official State Gazette (boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2013-10074), Articles 74 quater, 74 quinquies, 75 and 76; UGE holder guide v2 (holder guide); UGE management criterion DGGM 2/2025 (management criterion). programmes.overview:
Spain’s entrepreneur residence authorisation is for non-EU nationals over 18 who intend to establish, run or manage an innovative business of special economic interest to Spain. A favourable ENISA project report is mandatory. The programme operates under Articles 68 to 70 of Law 14/2013.
3 years: Initial residence authorisation.
Up to 20 days: Legal maximum for the residence decision after electronic filing; administrative silence provisions apply.
10 working days: Maximum for the ENISA report from the UGE request, assessed separately.
10 working days: Visa decision from abroad, subject to longer Schengen consultation.
No set minimum investment or jobs: The project is assessed on its merits.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse or partner: Spouse or person in an analogous affective relationship. An unmarried, unregistered partner shows at least 1 year of continuous cohabitation, unless there are common children.
Children: Minor children, and adult children who depend economically on the holder and have not formed their own family unit. Aged 18 to under 26 if they meet the UGE conditions: no income from work or public benefits, and enrolled in a qualifying course or registered as a job-seeker. Aged 26 or over: only with an incapacity that prevents them from being economically independent.
Parents and grandparents: Dependent ascendants show economic or physical dependence; over 80 is presumed. Family members may apply with the holder or later.
Family application: filed by the family member, the holder or the hiring entity; the same fee model applies to holder and dependants. These age and dependence rules come from the UGE family guidance.
Investment Routes
Develop an innovative business activity of special economic interest to Spain and obtain a favourable ENISA report. There is no prescribed minimum investment or job-creation threshold; the project is assessed on its merits.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Pay the fee through the Ministry’s payment form and keep the receipt reference.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
Programme details checked against Law 14/2013 (Spanish Official State Gazette) and the Spanish Inclusion Ministry’s Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit, accessed 15 October 2026.
Applicant and Project Requirements
[TABLE]
Condition | What the law and the UGE say
Who | A non-EU foreign national over 18, entering Spain or already holding a stay, residence or visa authorisation, who wants to start, run or manage a business activity (Articles 68 and 69).
The activity | An innovative activity of special economic interest for Spain, supported by a favourable report (Article 70).
The mandatory report | Issued by ENISA after the UGE requests it. It must say whether it is favourable or unfavourable, and is due within 10 working days of the request (Article 70). The applicant gives ENISA the profile, business plan and value-added information through the ENISA website.
What is assessed | (1) The applicant’s professional profile and involvement, including each partner’s participation. (2) The business plan: project, product or service, market, financing, investment required and funding sources. (3) The value added for the Spanish economy, such as innovation or an investment opportunity.
Investment and jobs | The UGE sets no minimum investment and no minimum job creation. The project is assessed on its merits.
General conditions | Over 18; no criminal record in Spain or in the countries lived in during the last 5 years; health insurance with an insurer authorised in Spain; sufficient economic resources; fee paid (Article 62.3).
[/TABLE]
Examples of Innovation
The UGE instruction gives examples a project can use to show innovation: recent public research and development funding, recognised awards, or the Innovative SME seal. These are examples only. The ENISA report may be unfavourable where there are reasonable doubts about reputational, regulatory, ethical or speculative risks.
The amount of economic resources to show is confirmed at proposal stage. “UGE” is the Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit of the Spanish Inclusion Ministry (Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos).
Application Process and Renewal

Program Overview
Spain’s entrepreneur residence authorisation is for non-EU nationals over 18 who intend to establish, run or manage an innovative business of special economic interest to Spain. A favourable ENISA project report is mandatory. The programme operates under Articles 68 to 70 of Law 14/2013.
3 years: Initial residence authorisation.
Up to 20 days: Legal maximum for the residence decision after electronic filing; administrative silence provisions apply.
10 working days: Maximum for the ENISA report from the UGE request, assessed separately.
10 working days: Visa decision from abroad, subject to longer Schengen consultation.
No set minimum investment or jobs: The project is assessed on its merits.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse or partner: Spouse or person in an analogous affective relationship. An unmarried, unregistered partner shows at least 1 year of continuous cohabitation, unless there are common children.
Children: Minor children, and adult children who depend economically on the holder and have not formed their own family unit. Aged 18 to under 26 if they meet the UGE conditions: no income from work or public benefits, and enrolled in a qualifying course or registered as a job-seeker. Aged 26 or over: only with an incapacity that prevents them from being economically independent.
Parents and grandparents: Dependent ascendants show economic or physical dependence; over 80 is presumed. Family members may apply with the holder or later.
Family application: filed by the family member, the holder or the hiring entity; the same fee model applies to holder and dependants. These age and dependence rules come from the UGE family guidance.
Investment Routes
Develop an innovative business activity of special economic interest to Spain and obtain a favourable ENISA report. There is no prescribed minimum investment or job-creation threshold; the project is assessed on its merits.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
Government Processing Fees
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Pay the fee through the Ministry’s payment form and keep the receipt reference.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.

Programme details checked against Law 14/2013 (Spanish Official State Gazette) and the Spanish Inclusion Ministry’s Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit, accessed 15 October 2026.

Condition | What the law and the UGE say
Who | A non-EU foreign national over 18, entering Spain or already holding a stay, residence or visa authorisation, who wants to start, run or manage a business activity (Articles 68 and 69).

ENISA report processing time | 10 working days from the UGE’s request (Article 70). This is a separate step. The two periods are not added together here.
Visa from abroad processing time | 10 working days, longer where the Schengen consultation applies (Article 75.5).
[/TABLE]

programmes.overview:
Spain’s Highly Qualified Professionals route allows a company or entity to apply for residence for a professional it hires. Under Article 71 of Law 14/2013, the route covers management and qualified staff of large companies, staff in projects of general interest, and graduates of renowned universities and business schools. The employer submits the application.
EUR 41,356.36: Minimum gross annual salary cited for 2026, with limited reductions subject to confirmation.
Up to 3 years: Initial residence authorisation; for shorter contracts, contract duration plus three months, capped at three years.
2 years: Renewal periods, subject to continuing eligibility.
Up to 20 days: Legal maximum for the residence decision from electronic filing.
10 working days: Visa decision from abroad, subject to longer Schengen consultation.
Who Can Be Included
Spouse or partner: Spouse or person in an analogous affective relationship. An unmarried, unregistered partner shows at least 1 year of continuous cohabitation, unless there are common children.
Children: Minor children, and adult children who depend economically on the holder and have not formed their own family unit. Aged 18 to under 26: no income from work or public benefits, and enrolled in a qualifying course or registered as a job-seeker. Aged 26 or over: only with an incapacity that prevents them from being economically independent.
Parents and grandparents: Dependent ascendants show economic or physical dependence; over 80 is presumed. Family members may apply with the holder or later.
Family application: filed by the family member, the holder or the hiring entity; the same fee model applies to holder and dependants. These age and dependence rules come from the UGE family guidance.
Family members apply with the Ministry’s family application form and must show sufficient economic resources. The amount is confirmed at proposal stage.
Applicant and Employer Eligibility
[TABLE]
Condition | What the law and the Ministry say
Category (a) | Management or highly qualified staff of large companies or groups.
Category (b) | Staff in projects of general interest, certified by the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investments.
Category (c) | Graduates and postgraduates of renowned universities and business schools.
Employer application | The employer applies; the professional cannot apply alone.
Company tests (category a) | The employer meets one of: more than 250 workers in Spain; annual net turnover over EUR 50 million (or own funds over EUR 43 million); average gross inward investment of at least EUR 1 million over the previous 3 years; or an investment stock over EUR 3 million. Small and medium businesses in a strategic sector, certified by the Directorate-General, can also qualify.
Company registration | The company’s registration with the UGE is valid for 3 years and renewable. Any change must be notified within 30 days.
Qualification | National route: a degree comparable to Level 1 of the Spanish higher education framework, or 3 years of equivalent professional experience. EU Blue Card route: a Level 2 qualification (at least 3 years of higher education) or 5 years of comparable experience, plus a job contract or firm offer of at least 6 months.
Minimum salary | The contract or firm job offer must state a gross annual salary of at least EUR 41,356.36. This is 1.4 times the average annual gross salary per worker published by the Spanish statistics institute (Orden PJC/44/2026).
Salary updates | The amount is updated by the Ministry when a new salary survey is published, and applies to applications filed from one month after publication. A reduced threshold applies in limited cases; it is confirmed at proposal stage. The figure is correct at 15 October 2026.
General conditions | Over 18, no criminal record, health insurance, sufficient resources and the fee paid (Article 62.3).
[/TABLE]
Tax Advice
Elevay does not provide tax advice. Tax residence and personal tax treatment are separate from the immigration assessment. Obtain independent tax advice before applying.

Accessed 15 October 2026.
Sources: Law 14/2013, consolidated text (English translation, inclusion.gob.es; Spanish text at boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2013-10074), Articles 62.4 and 62.5; Migration Sheet 66; UGE application page (sede.inclusion.gob.es/en/w/presentacion-solicitudes-autorizacion-residencia); UGE family guidance. Accessed 15 October 2026.
Investment Routes
No qualifying investment is required under this route.
Contribution Options
No separate contribution route applies.
The law applies without prejudice to the applicant’s tax and Social Security obligations (Article 62.5).
Government Processing Fees
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Fee paid (Article 62.3). The same fee model applies to holder and dependants.
Due Diligence Fees
No separate due diligence fee is specified. Any applicable fees will be confirmed at the proposal stage.
Travel Access
This programme concerns residence rather than the grant of citizenship or a passport.
Residence and Application Details
[TABLE]
Item | Detail
Minimum salary in the contract or job offer (2026) | EUR 41,356.36 a year, gross.
Initial authorisation | The length of the employment contract plus 3 months if the contract is shorter than 3 years. It never exceeds 3 years. It allows residence and work throughout Spain (Article 71.3; Sheet 66).
Renewal | Renewals run in 2-year periods while the conditions that gave the right still hold (Sheet 67). Renewal is never promised.
When to apply | During the 60 calendar days before expiry. A late application is possible within 90 calendar days after expiry, although a sanction procedure may be opened. A timely application extends the old authorisation until a decision.
Identity card | After a renewal, request the foreigner identity card in person within one month of notification.
Residence authorisation processing time | A maximum of 20 days from electronic filing. If no decision is made in that time, the authorisation is deemed granted by administrative silence (Sheet 66; Article 76.1).
Visa from abroad | 10 working days, longer where the Schengen consultation applies (Article 75.5).
[/TABLE]
Legal maximums exclude document preparation and do not guarantee approval or renewal.

programmes.overview:
Spain’s Non-Lucrative Residence authorisation is for eligible non-EU nationals with sufficient personal means to live in Spain without working. Applications are submitted through the Spanish consulate responsible for the applicant’s place of residence. The route operates under Organic Law 4/2000 and Royal Decree 1155/2024.
EUR 28,800: Main applicant’s annual gross means requirement, calculated from 400% of IPREM.
1 year: Initial validity from entry into Spain.
Up to 1 month: Legal decision maximum from the consulate’s communication.
No work permitted: Employment and professional activity are excluded.
Who Can Be Included
A spouse or registered or proven stable partner and children under 18 may be included in the application.
Children: under 18. Adult children only with a disability that prevents them from supporting themselves (Article 17 of Organic Law 4/2000, the general family rule).
Each dependant adds 100% of IPREM to the financial requirement: EUR 7,200 a year, gross. School-age children must also meet the enrolment requirement. Family documentation will be presented at the proposal stage.
Applicant Eligibility and Financial Means
[TABLE]
Condition | What the Ministry says
Who | Not an EU, EEA or Swiss citizen or a family member covered by the EU citizen regime; over 18; not in Spain irregularly.
Health | Public or private health insurance with an insurer authorised in Spain, plus a medical certificate. No serious disease under the 2005 International Health Regulations.
Criminal record | No criminal record in Spain or in the countries lived in during the last 5 years, for offences punishable under Spanish law.
Public order | No threat to public order, security or health, and no active commitment not to return to Spain.
No work | The authorisation does not allow work or professional activity. If your funds come from a company, the company certifies that you do not work there and you give a sworn statement to the same effect.
Main applicant means | 400% of the IPREM. With the IPREM at EUR 600 a month, that is EUR 2,400 a month, or EUR 28,800 a year (12 months, gross).
Each dependant means | 100% of the IPREM for each dependant: EUR 7,200 a year (12 months, gross).
[/TABLE]
The IPREM is the Spanish public reference income indicator. It is EUR 600 a month under Law 31/2022, the latest figure in the Social Security table at 15 October 2026. The Ministry sheet states the requirement per month; the annual figures are calculated over 12 months. The means must be enough to live without working.
Sources: Migration Sheet 6 (inclusion.gob.es/en/web/migraciones/w/autorizacion-inicial-de-residencia-temporal-no-lucrativa, updated May 2025); Social Security IPREM table (seg-social.es) and Law 31/2022 (BOE). Accessed 15 October 2026.

This is a legal maximum, not a promise. At this initial stage, if no decision is issued in that time the request is considered rejected. Nothing in this summary guarantees that an application will be approved.
After the visa is granted, collect the visa within 1 month and enter Spain within its validity (at most 3 months). Within 1 month of entry, apply in person for the foreigner identity card. Foreign documents need a sworn translation and an apostille or legalisation, unless exempt.

[TABLE]
Item | Detail
Conditions | Means enough to live without working, family included; health insurance kept in force; school-age children enrolled; more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year; no criminal record.
Validity | 2 years, unless a long-term residence permit is more appropriate.

Decision | 3 months from filing. If no decision is notified, the renewal may be considered approved by administrative silence.

programmes.name: UAE Golden Visa
programmes.cardSummary: A federation of seven emirates offering long-term residence to qualifying investors through the Golden Visa.
programmes.overview:
The UAE Golden Visa provides long-term residence for qualifying investors in real estate, financial deposits, company capital or partnership shares, or businesses meeting the federal tax threshold. The investor residence is valid for ten years and may be renewed while the conditions continue to be met. No sponsor is required.
10 years: Residence validity, renewable subject to continued eligibility.
AED 2,000,000: Minimum for the real estate, deposit and company investment routes.
4 routes: Real estate, financial deposit, company investment and federal tax paid.
Extended absence permitted: Golden Residence holders are exempt from the usual 180-day absence rule, subject to the authority’s conditions.
Applications are handled by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (ICP), Dubai Land Department (DLD) and General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs — Dubai (GDRFA), as applicable. Approval and renewal are not guaranteed.
Who Can Be Included
The spouse of the main applicant
Children
Parents
ICP states that children may be sponsored regardless of age. DLD requires an undertaking that sons and daughters over 18 are unmarried. If the sponsor dies, sponsored family members may remain for the validity of their permits, according to ICP.
Investment Routes
Option 1 — Real Estate
Invest in property or properties in the UAE with a total value of at least AED 2,000,000, fully owned and registered in the investor’s name, according to ICP.
[TABLE]
Condition | Requirement
Off-plan property | Units purchased from an approved local developer may qualify where the total is at least AED 2,000,000 (ICP).
Joint ownership | The investor’s share must itself be worth at least AED 2,000,000 (GDRFA).
Valuation | A DLD property status certificate certifies the value. GDRFA also accepts a valuation certificate from a DLD-licensed office. DLD describes a purchase value of at least AED 2,000,000 at the time of purchase.
Mortgaged property | Accepted, subject to a bank letter showing the amount paid and the outstanding balance (DLD).
Holding period | GDRFA states that the property may not be disposed of during the ten-year residence period and that a lien applies throughout that period.
Renewal | The requirements for issuance must continue to be met when renewal is requested (ICP).
[/TABLE]
Investment Options
Option 2 — Financial Deposit
Deposit at least AED 2,000,000 in an eligible investment fund or national bank operating in the UAE, according to ICP. GDRFA specifies an accredited local bank and allows local sukuk or investment bonds. The funds must be fully owned by the investor and not derived from a loan, with evidence of their source and ownership.
Deposit Holding Conditions
GDRFA requires the bank certificate to show a freeze of at least two years. It also states that the deposit or investment cannot be withdrawn or refunded during the ten-year Golden Residency period. Both conditions appear in the cited authority wording. ICP states no deposit holding period in the supplied material.
Option 3 — Company Capital or Partner Share
Invest at least AED 2,000,000 in company capital or a partner’s financial share. ICP requires the capital to be fully owned and not derived from a loan. GDRFA requires the investor’s share of company assets to be worth at least AED 2,000,000, supported by a certified financial report from a UAE-accredited audit firm.
Option 4 — Federal Tax Paid
Qualify as the owner or partner of a company paying at least AED 250,000 in federal taxes annually. Under ICP’s wording, a partner’s shareholding must correspond to at least AED 250,000 of annual tax paid.
GDRFA requires evidence that at least AED 250,000 in taxes was paid in the last year or the fiscal year before application, supported by a Federal Tax Authority letter and a trade licence with the partners’ appendix.
Government Processing Fees
All applicable fees will be presented at the proposal stage.
Health Insurance
The investor and family members must have comprehensive and valid health insurance. ICP requires coverage at application for the public-investment routes and throughout the residence period for real estate.
Residence and Renewal
GDRFA states that Golden Residence holders are exempt from the 180-day residency rule and that residence becomes void if it expires outside the country. The UAE government portal states that holders may remain abroad for longer than the usual six months. These statements do not mean absence is unlimited.
The authorities may check continued eligibility throughout the permit’s validity. Maintain all applicable requirements when requesting renewal. Your Elevay consultant will confirm the documents and conditions applicable to your route.
Sources
ICP, Dubai Land Department and GDRFA official programme pages, accessed 19 October 2026; u.ae, About the UAE and Golden Visa information; World Bank surface area, population and GDP per capita indicators. GDP per capita is a national average, not a measure of individual income.
Family Scope of Figures
Each investment, contribution, income or fee figure applies only to the applicant or family composition stated beside that figure. If no family size is stated, the programme information does not specify one.
